2607.28068.title: Stimulus-Evoked Network Dynamics in Human Cortical Organoids: From a Graph-Computational Framework to Repeated-Stimulation Depression
2607.28068.paper_summary: Human cortical organoids provide an experimentally accessible model of early neural circuit formation, yet whether their activity reflects structured information processing rather than spontaneous synchronization is unclear. We developed a graph-computational framework to quantify stimulus-evoked propagation. This includes stimulus-conditioned functional graphs, a graph-constrained dynamical (graph-neural-network) model used as a system-identification tool, a biological message-passing principle bounding integration depth by observable propagation depth, and a suite of graph-level metrics. We carried this program out in full on longitudinal HD-MEA recordings from three organoids. Once the true acquisition sampling rate and stimulus timing were recovered, the evoked response proved to be a fast, near-synchronous network burst with no measurable outward propagation (peak-latency vs. distance slope = 0). The propagation/integration-depth metrics (Deff ,reachability index, dmax) therefore do not apply, and per-day connectivity graphs were not reliably estimable at the available trial count, a negative result with methodological consequences for applying such metrics to organoid data. Reframing around synchrony, response-population size and shared variability revealed a control-validated phenomenon, i.e., repeated daily stimulation progressively depressed and spatially contracted the evoked response. That repeated stimulation reshapes organoid networks is established, but longitudinal designs in which every preparation is stimulated cannot separate this from developmental maturation. We break that confound with a developmentally-matched, stimulation-naive control, where at day 7, an organoid receiving its first-ever stimulation engaged 93% of the array, whereas organoids with five prior sessions engaged 10%.
2607.28068.paper_summary_zh: 人類皮質類器官提供了一個可實驗訪問的早期神經電路形成模型，但它們的活動是否反映了結構化的信息處理而非自發的同步仍不清楚。<lb/>我們開發了一個圖計算框架來量化刺激引發的傳播。<lb/>這包括刺激條件下的功能圖、一個作為系統識別工具的圖約束動態（圖神經網絡）模型、一個生物信息傳遞原則，該原則通過可觀察的傳播深度限制整合深度，以及一套圖層級指標。<lb/>我們在來自三個類器官的長期 HD-MEA 記錄中全面執行了這個計劃。<lb/>一旦恢復了真實的獲取取樣率和刺激時機，所引發的反應證明是一個快速、近同步的網絡爆發，沒有可測量的外向傳播（峰值延遲與距離斜率 = 0）。<lb/>因此，傳播/整合深度指標（Deff、可達性指數、dmax）不適用，且每日連通性圖在可用的試驗數量下無法可靠估算，這對於將此類指標應用於類器官數據具有方法學上的負面影響。<lb/>圍繞同步性、反應群體大小和共享變異性重新框架揭示了一個經過控制驗證的現象，即重複的每日刺激逐漸抑制並空間上收縮了所引發的反應。<lb/>重複刺激重塑類器官網絡是已確立的，但每個準備都受到刺激的縱向設計無法將其與發展成熟分開。<lb/>我們通過一個發展上匹配、未受刺激的對照來打破這一混淆，在第 7 天，一個首次接受刺激的類器官使 93% 的陣列參與，而有五次先前刺激的類器官則使 10% 的陣列參與。
